newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions agree to fresh talks on reforms.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions agree to fresh talks on reforms.

text.p: Argentine union leaders on Wednesday approved plans to begin a fresh round of talks with the government on labor reforms adamantly opposed by workers.
The CGT labor federation's board decided formally to accept a proposal by President Carlos Menem's administration to restart talks on plans to change working conditions in Argentina.

The state-run Telam news agency reported the two sides agreed to meet on Thursday. It quoted CGT chief Rodolfo Daer as saying he, the cabinet chief and the labor and interior ministers agreed to begin talks at 1230 local/1530 GMT.
Daer said at a news conference after the board meeting that the unions would also seek to discuss other issues affecting union members.
"We want to discuss other problems affecting workers, such as the tax system, the state of the regional economies and the situation of medium- and small-sized businesses," he said.
Menem's government decided to invite unions back to the negotiation table after two judges blocked its attempt to introduce the labor reforms by presidential decrees.

The decrees would have let smaller companies bypass national unions in collective pay talks and allow companies to appeal to the government if they wanted to negotiate with trade unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.

Arguing that "flexibilization" of labor was the best way to tackle 17.3 percent unemployment, Menem resorted to the decrees in the face of congressional opposition and a breakdown in talks with unions, which fear their power is under threat.
The CGT staged a 24-hour general strike on December 26, its third last year.

The Peronist government at first threatened to impeach the the first judge who ruled the decrees were unconstitutional. But it later toned down the debate by saying it would not attempt to impeach the second judge and indicating it would comply with the higher courts if they rejected its appeals.
